text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and automated builds start immediately. These builds compile the code and run tests to check that everything works correctly. By testing every change, teams can catch issues early, before they become serious problems. This makes fixing bugs faster and easier. CI pipelines help organise these steps, from building the software to running automated tests. As a result, developers receive quick feedback and can improve code quality. Ultimately, Continuous Integration helps teams work together more efficiently and deliver reliable software more often.
